record.paper_title: A List of Problems on the Reverse Mathematics of Ramsey Theory on the Rado Graph and on Infinite, Finitely Branching Trees
record.original_question: Does the reverse-mathematical strength of Milliken theorem depend on the height of the finite trees being colored?

evidence.quote: (7) Does the strength of the Milliken Theorem depend on the height of the finite trees being colored?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background. A tree here is a finitely-branching, rooted, infinite tree T with no leaves. For a node x in T, the height of x is the length of the unique path from the root to x. For each n ≥ 1, a strong subtree of T of height n is a subset S ⊆ T together with a chosen set of "level nodes" {ℓ_0 < ℓ_1 < … < ℓ_{n-1}} of T such that S = {s ∈ T : s extends some node of S at level ℓ_i for some i < n}, every node of S at level ℓ_i has exactly the same set of immediate successors (in T) extended into S at level ℓ_{i+1}, and S has a single root.

For each n ≥ 1, let MTT_n denote the following statement (Milliken's tree theorem at height n): for every finitely-branching, infinite, leafless tree T, every positive integer k, and every coloring f : S_n(T) → k of the set S_n(T) of strong subtrees of T of height n with k colors, there exists an infinite strong subtree T' ⊆ T such that f is constant on S_n(T').

Working over the base theory RCA_0 of reverse mathematics, determine whether the proof-theoretic strength of MTT_n depends on the parameter n. More precisely: is there any pair of integers m, n ≥ 1 such that MTT_m and MTT_n are not equivalent over RCA_0? Equivalently, does the sequence of principles (MTT_n)_{n≥1} stabilize in strength at some finite level, and if so at what level?
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent work (notably Anglès d'Auriac–Cholak–Dzhafarov–Monin–Patey, "Milliken's tree theorem and its applications: a computability-theoretic perspective," arXiv:2007.09739) gives a comprehensive classification of the computable content of Milliken's tree theorem and analyzes the principles MTT_n for varying n, providing substantial information on how the strength of MTT_n behaves with n. Whether the exact reverse-mathematical strength is the same for all n (i.e., the full equivalence picture over RCA_0) is addressed there but related fine-grained questions (e.g. comparisons with TT_n^k) remain open.

status_evidence.title: Milliken's tree theorem and its applications: a computability-theoretic perspective
status_evidence.snippet: A careful analysis of the Halpern-Laüchli theorem ... permits gauging its effectivity, with the principal outcome being a comprehensive classification of the computable content of Milliken's tree theorem.
status_evidence.claim: Provides a comprehensive computability-theoretic classification of MTT, addressing how its strength behaves with height parameter n.

status_evidence.title: The strength of the tree theorem for pairs in reverse mathematics
status_evidence.snippet: Studies the strength of tree theorem for pairs over RCA_0.
status_evidence.claim: Related work on the reverse-math strength of tree theorems at specific heights.
